entitySuffixRule: Must end with the words "limited liability company" or the upper- or lower-case letters "l.l.c." (with or without punctuation). A low-profit LLC ends with "low-profit, limited liability company" or the abbreviation "L3C" or "13c." Rhode Island does not accept "limited company," "LC," or "L.C."
distinguishabilityNote: Must be distinguishable upon the records of the Secretary of State from the name of any corporation, non-business corporation or other association, limited partnership, or domestic or foreign limited liability company organized, registered, or qualified in Rhode Island, and from any name filed, reserved, or registered under Title 7. Statutory entity-type designators are disregarded when comparing names. The Secretary of State issues rules defining "distinguishable upon the record." Two escapes exist: the requirement does not apply if the applicant files a certified copy of a final decree of a court of competent jurisdiction establishing the applicant's prior right to the name in Rhode Island, and the name may be the same as that of an entity whose certificate the Secretary of State has revoked, once a year has passed without the revocation being withdrawn.
nameReservationCostBasis: The reservation fee is $50 (Form 620); a $2.50 enhanced-access fee is added to online filings, so the online cost is $52.50.
notes: Rhode Island's LLC Act (R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 7-16) puts naming and fictitious names in a single section, § 7-16-9: the entity name rules are subsection (a) and the fictitious business name regime is subsection (b). The name must end with "limited liability company" or "l.l.c." (Rhode Island does not accept "limited company," "LC," or "L.C."), or the L3C form for a low-profit LLC. Entity-type designators are disregarded in the distinguishability comparison, and § 7-16-9(a)(2)(ii) gives two escapes from it: a court decree of prior right, or an entity name the Secretary of State revoked more than a year ago. The reservation lasts 120 days; § 7-16-10 provides for transfer of the reserved name but no renewal. Rhode Island's costs run high: LLC formation is $150 ($156 online) and the annual report is $50 ($52.50 online), due between February 1 and May 1.
